summaryBox.title: Type Specimens Concept
summaryBox.takeaway: Nomenclatural types anchor abstract scientific descriptions to real physical specimens preserved in herbaria or natural history museums worldwide.

conceptBreakdown.content: Taxonomic descriptions must be anchored to concrete physical specimens. When a new species is published, specific type specimens must be designated:

listPills.title: Holotype
listPills.text: The single physical specimen designated by the original author at the time of publishing the species description as the official nomenclatural type.

listPills.title: Isotype
listPills.text: An exact duplicate specimen of the holotype collected from the same individual/population, at the same time, by the same collector (very common in botanical collections).

listPills.title: Paratype
listPills.text: Any specimen cited in the original protologue/description other than the holotype or isotype.

listPills.title: Lectotype
listPills.text: A specimen chosen from the original collection material to serve as the single nomenclatural type when no holotype was originally designated, or if the original holotype was lost or destroyed.

listPills.title: Neotype
listPills.text: A replacement specimen chosen to serve as the nomenclatural type when ALL original material (holotype, isotypes, syntypes) has been lost or destroyed.

listPills.title: Topotype
listPills.text: A specimen collected from the exact original geographic type locality where the original type specimen was obtained.

listPills.title: Syntype
listPills.text: Any one of two or more specimens cited by an author when no single holotype was designated in the original publication.

quickRevision: Isotype = exact duplicate of holotype collected at same time/place.
Lectotype = selected from original material if holotype lost/unassigned.
Neotype = replacement when ALL original material destroyed.
Topotype = collected from original type locality.
